ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Flannery O'Connor Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for joint pain and swelling, fevers, fatigue, a facial rash, and protein in the urine in a writer of 25. Concerns: Painful, swollen hands and knees, fevers, tiredness, and a rash on her face, for three months; Wants a plain, complete answer about what is wrong, told to her directly, and asks that it not be shared with anyone she has not named; Afraid of losing her writing mornings to illness or treatment. [S]

Two tablets up to every 8 hours as needed
Hydroxychloroquine sulfate 300 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily (5 mg/kg of actual body weight), long term
Losartan potassium 25 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily, for proteinuria and blood pressure
Methylprednisolone 500 mg intravenous infusion once daily for three days
One infusion daily for three days
Prednisone 5 mg oral tablet: 30 mg (six tablets) once daily from the day after the last pulse, reduced by 5 mg every two weeks to 10 mg, then to 5 mg a day or less by six months
Mycophenolate mofetil 500 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice daily for one week, then two tablets (1000 mg) twice daily
Belimumab 200 mg/mL subcutaneous autoinjector: 400 mg (two injections) once weekly for four doses, then 200 mg once weekly
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 1000 units oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily
Nitrofurantoin (monohydrate/macrocrystals) 100 mg oral capsule, one capsule by mouth twice daily with food for seven days
One capsule twice daily for seven days

list.item: Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established: resolved, confirmed [S]
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established: resolved, confirmed [S]

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative: active, confirmed [S]

Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class III (A), focal proliferative, on kidney biopsy: endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, full-house immunofluorescence; no thrombotic microangiopathy; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g; normal kidney function: active, confirmed [S]
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less: active, confirmed [S]
Long-term mycophenolate mofetil, with belimumab, for lupus nephritis; bone and infection protection in place: active, confirmed [S]
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system for highly effective contraception during mycophenolate treatment: active, confirmed [S]

Acute cystitis on mycophenolate, belimumab, and prednisone 15 mg: two days of burning, frequency, and urgency without fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved with seven days of nitrofurantoin: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Primary care visit for joint pain and swelling, fevers, fatigue, a facial rash, and protein in the urine in a writer of 25
Diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus with the rheumatology consultation the same day; vaccinations before immunosuppression
Kidney biopsy result: class III lupus nephritis; start of pulse methylprednisolone, prednisone, mycophenolate, and belimumab
Three-month response assessment for lupus nephritis and glucocorticoid taper
Six-month response assessment: complete renal response; prednisone 5 mg; pregnancy planning
Same-day sick visit for bladder symptoms on immunosuppression

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Inflammatory arthritis with fever, rash, cytopenias, and an abnormal urine: blood count, chemistry, ESR and CRP, urine microscopy and protein-to-creatinine ratio today; ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, complements, and antiphospholipid antibodies; no NSAIDs with protein in the urine
Rheumatology consultation within ten days, to confirm the diagnosis, stage organ involvement, and plan treatment with her
Disclosure: every result explained to her directly and in plain words, with a written copy; her health shared only with the people she names
Sun protection: broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 50 or higher, a wide-brimmed hat, and shade in the middle of the day
Hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily (5 mg/kg) for every patient with lupus, long term, with a baseline eye examination within the first year and yearly screening after five years
Kidney biopsy for proteinuria above 0.5 g/g with an active sediment, to class the nephritis before treatment

Vaccinations before immunosuppression: PCV20 and recombinant zoster dose 1 now, zoster dose 2 after one to two months, seasonal influenza and COVID-19; no live vaccines on immunosuppression; hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV screening
Angiotensin receptor blocker (losartan) for proteinuria and blood pressure, target below 130/80 mmHg, with potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after starting

Contraception before mycophenolate: highly effective method of her choice (levonorgestrel intrauterine system); pregnancy test before starting; pregnancy planning later for at least six months of quiet disease on pregnancy-compatible medicines

Class III lupus nephritis: methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for three days, then prednisone 30 mg tapered to 5 mg a day or less by six months; mycophenolate mofetil 2 g a day with belimumab, continued for three to five years after a complete response; blood counts weekly for the first month, twice monthly for the next two, then monthly; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, urine sediment, creatinine, anti-dsDNA, and complements every three months

Bone protection on glucocorticoids: baseline DXA, vitamin D3 and calcium from food, weight-bearing exercise; report new hip, groin, or knee pain at once so avascular necrosis can be looked for with MRI
Cardiovascular risk: blood pressure at every visit, lipids and HbA1c at three months on glucocorticoids, no smoking, activity, and a lower glucocorticoid dose

Writing life: treatment visits and infusions booked in the afternoons, belimumab self-injected at home, fatigue managed with graded activity and sleep; her illness kept out of conversations about her work unless she chooses otherwise
Establish the diagnosis within two weeks and hear it directly, in plain words
Told directly at nine days that she has systemic lupus erythematosus, with the reasons and a written summary
Renal response: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio halved by three months and below 0.5 g/g with stable kidney function by six to twelve months
Ratio 1.8 at diagnosis, 0.9 at three months, 0.35 at six months, a complete response; creatinine 0.8 throughout
Prednisone 5 mg a day or less by six months, with withdrawal considered later
5 mg a day at six months
Write at least four mornings a week through treatment
Writing five mornings a week by three months
No unplanned pregnancy on mycophenolate; plan any pregnancy for a time of quiet disease on compatible medicines
Intrauterine system in place; pregnancy planning discussed
